guide.summary: The Duomo, Leonardo's Last Supper and Milan's picture galleries and house museums, with breakfast pastry shops, trattorias, markets and cocktail bars checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: The Last Supper and Pinacoteca di Brera both close on Mondays and both require a reservation, so book them for Tuesday to Sunday before you fix the rest of your days.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: Pinacoteca di Brera closes every Monday and The Last Supper opens Tuesday to Sunday only. Pirelli HangarBicocca's exhibitions are closed Monday to Wednesday, and Museo Bagatti Valsecchi opens Wednesday to Sunday.

toolkit.label: Tickets and booking
toolkit.copy: The Last Supper says reservations are compulsory for all ticket types, with 15-minute visits for up to 40 people, and releases tickets three months at a time. Pinacoteca di Brera also requires a reservation, including on its free first Sunday of the month.

toolkit.label: Walk-in or book
toolkit.copy: Café Cracco in the Galleria does not take reservations and opens daily 8am to midnight. Ratanà books online for up to eight people, and a booking only counts once you receive the confirmation email.

toolkit.label: Free entry rules
toolkit.copy: Pirelli HangarBicocca is free but asks you to book your admission online. Brera's first-Sunday free entry also needs a reservation.

guide.dek: Book The Last Supper and Brera first, keep Mondays for markets, pastry shops and Thursday-to-Sunday spaces like HangarBicocca, and reserve dinners ahead.
intro: Milan's headline sights reward a little planning. At The Last Supper in Santa Maria delle Grazie, reservations are compulsory for every ticket type, visits last 15 minutes with up to 40 people, and the museum opens Tuesday to Sunday from 8.15am to 7pm. Tickets are released three months at a time, so check the sales calendar early. Pinacoteca di Brera, on Via Brera, also asks you to reserve, opens Tuesday to Sunday from 8.30am to 7.15pm with last entry at 6pm, and is free with a reservation on the first Sunday of each month.

Several exhibitions run well into winter. Brera's "100 Years for Brera", on gifts and acquisitions from its Friends, runs from 6 October 2026 to 14 February 2027. The Pinacoteca Ambrosiana on Piazza Pio XI shows "The 'Sign' of Saint Francis: Images of a Life" until 12 January 2027, and the Museo Diocesano at Piazza Sant'Eustorgio shows Artemisia Gentileschi's "Annunciazione" from 27 October 2026 to 31 January 2027. Further out, Pirelli HangarBicocca on Via Chiese is free with booking, opens Thursday to Sunday from 10.30am to 8.30pm, and shows Aki Sasamoto until 17 January 2027 and Luciano Fabro until 21 February 2027.

For a quieter day, Museo Bagatti Valsecchi on Via Gesù opens Wednesday to Sunday from 10am to 6pm and recommends booking online, while FAI's Villa Necchi Campiglio on Via Mozart says its Piero Portaluppi drawing exhibition has been extended to 29 November. Mornings start easily: Café Cracco in the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II opens daily from 8am and takes no reservations, Pasticceria Martesana in Piazza Sant'Agostino opens from 7.30am on weekdays, and Biffi on Corso Magenta opens every day from 7am. Luini on Via Santa Radegonda serves Monday to Saturday, 10am to 8pm.

Evenings need more booking. Ratanà on Via de Castillia is open every day for lunch and dinner, takes online bookings for up to eight, and treats a booking as valid only once you receive a confirmation email. Antica Trattoria della Pesa on Viale Pasubio is closed on Sundays, and Ristorante Cracco serves dinner Monday to Saturday and lunch Tuesday to Friday. For drinks, Camparino in Galleria's Bar di Passo opens from 9.30am, Dry Milano on Via Solferino opens Tuesday to Sunday from 6pm to 2am, and Ally's Bar, on the sixth floor of Langosteria Montenapoleone, runs from noon to 1am.
summaryCards: Pair the Duomo with a reserved Tuesday-to-Sunday slot at The Last Supper and a booked visit to Pinacoteca di Brera.
Start with pastries at Pasticceria Martesana or Biffi, then spend the late morning at Museo Bagatti Valsecchi or Museo Poldi Pezzoli.
Remember that Brera and The Last Supper close on Mondays and HangarBicocca's exhibitions open only Thursday to Sunday.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Several major sites could not be read by automated fetch (HTTP 403 for Castello Sforzesco, Museo del Novecento, Fondazione Prada, Palazzo Reale, Triennale, GAM and the City of Milan's Parco Sempione page; certificate or TLS errors for Bar Basso, Pizzeria Spontini, Princi and Cova; repeated HTTP 429 for Pasticceria Cucchi, Iginio Massari and Cafezal; timeout for Pasticceria Marchesi), so they are left out rather than judged closed. The Duomo's ticket site sits behind a queue system that was not bypassed, so cathedral and terrace opening hours and dress rules were not confirmed; the main site's weekday hours may refer to the office. Weekly hours were not published on the pages read for Pinacoteca Ambrosiana, Villa Necchi Campiglio, Museo Diocesano, MUBA, Peck and Langosteria (Via Savona), and Museo Poldi Pezzoli showed only today's hours. Camparino, Dry Milano, Moebius, Luini, Antica Trattoria della Pesa, Masuelli and Biffi showed current hours or booking but no 2026-dated content. Two fetch summaries (museoscienza.org and trattoriamilanese.it) reported text addressed to an AI that could not be quoted and appeared to echo the review prompt; neither place is used.
